paragraph: The Ministry of Finance [launched and runs the Portal do Munícipe under Presidential Decree 47/18](<https://radionova.co.ao/ministerio-das-financas-lanca-portal-para-aumentar-nivel-de-arrecadacao-de-receitas-das-administracoes-locais/>). On 10 November 2021 its Secretary of State said [the Portal was implemented in all 164 municipalities, with telecommunications problems in some](<https://radionova.co.ao/ministerio-das-financas-lanca-portal-para-aumentar-nivel-de-arrecadacao-de-receitas-das-administracoes-locais/>). No share or count of municipalities whose staff record in it has been found. Nothing dated after November 2021 has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

The Interior ministry [developed E-taxe, with CRDB Bank as collection interface](<https://mininterinfos.gov.bi/lancement-officiel-de-la-digitalisation-dans-la-collecte-des-recettes-communales-e-taxe/>), which began in 12 pilot communes on 23 August 2024. Its third-quarter report for 2025/26 [lists 30 communes digitalised in communal revenue](<https://finances.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CANEVAS-RAPPORT_MIDCSP_2025-2026_T3.xlsx>) and gives no total. In the last twelve months, VNG International said in September 2026 that [Nyanza had put its taxpayer information into its accounting software](<https://www.vng-international.nl/project/sdlg-burundi/>). It is the only commune shown with a register of payers. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of communes keep a digital register of payers.

In September 2019 the PAACOL project, [coordinated by the AIMF and implemented with the ANCB, the communes' association](<https://www.ancb.bj/index.php/projet/paacol.html>), had [selected 12 of Benin's 77 communes to be equipped with the cash windows](<https://www.ancb.bj/index.php/projet/paacol.html>). The cash-desk software records each payment, and the equipping was due during 2019/2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Whether the 12 communes were equipped and their cash desks went into use has not been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

The commune of Ouagadougou [runs SYSCOTAX for local taxes through its tax base office](<https://digitalmagazine.bf/2024/03/23/paiement-digital-des-taxes-ouagadougou-lance-la-syscotax-dans-4-marches/>), launched in four pilot markets on 19 March 2024. On 19 November 2025 its tax-base director said SYSCOTAX [records market traders by phone number and tracks who has paid what](<https://libreinfo.net/ouagadougou-la-commune-sensibilise-les-commercants-au-paiement-electronique-des-taxes/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No commune outside Ouagadougou has been found recording its revenue digitally, and no source says where the capital's record is kept. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

An agreement was signed with the Mairie de Bangui in December 2025. Under it, [BMI-WFS, a firm under Ivorian law, is to run the city's digital collection system](<https://acap-rca.com/2025/12/18/bangui-signature-dune-convention-pour-la-digitalisation-des-recettes-municipales/>). In the last twelve months, the only change found is that agreement, signed on 12 December 2025. Before it, a city-centre trader told RFI in December 2020 that [Bangui town hall had no computerised file of taxpayers](<https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/afrique-%C3%A9conomie/20201201-centrafrique-la-mairie-de-bangui-modernise-la-collecte-des-taxes-aupr%C3%A8s-des-commer%C3%A7ants>). No source says the system is in use, and no commune other than Bangui is named. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

The Directorate General of Decentralisation and Local Development [developed the SYGIDAN Recettes software in its own services](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-vers-la-digitalisation-des-recettes-fiscales-des-communes/>). It was at pre-validation in April 2024. The African Development Bank's appraisal of July 2021 places its pilot in [22 of 201 municipalities](<https://www.afdb.org/sites/default/files/documents/projects-and-operations/cote_divoire_-_pilot_support_for_the_mobilisation_of_municipal_revenue_pamrec_-_project_appraisal_report.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 9 December 2025 the directorate [handed the commune of Assinie-Mafia its taxpayer database, within the PAMREC pilot](<https://mairieassinie.com/web/ceremonie-de-restitution-des-bases-de-donnees-des-contribuables/>). No fact has been found saying the system is in use in any commune, or giving a count of communes recording. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

The AIMF reports that [FEICOM presented Inform'All City, a platform for collecting local tax from informal traders, on 21 March 2023](<https://www.aimf.asso.fr/actualite/au-cameroun-une-plateforme-numerique-pour-faciliter-la-collecte-des-taxes-aupres-des-commercants-informels/>). Informal traders register and pay on it. It [was to be deployed first in the councils of Yaoundé II and Douala III](<https://www.aimf.asso.fr/actualite/au-cameroun-une-plateforme-numerique-pour-faciliter-la-collecte-des-taxes-aupres-des-commercants-informels/>), in the political and economic capitals. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Whether the platform was deployed in any council, and where its record is held, has not been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

The digital tools for the decentralised territorial entities are [supported by USAID's Good Governance Activity, launched in July 2023](<https://cd.usembassy.gov/les-etats-unis-appuient-les-efforts-visant-a-ameliorer-la-gestion-des-finances-publiques-des-entites-territoriales-decentralisees-etd/>). A workshop of 23 to 24 July 2024 was [to standardise and assess tools for tracking revenue, registering taxpayers and budgeting](<https://cd.usembassy.gov/les-etats-unis-appuient-les-efforts-visant-a-ameliorer-la-gestion-des-finances-publiques-des-entites-territoriales-decentralisees-etd/>), with 20 entities in four provinces. No change has been found in the last twelve months. What the tools record, where the record is held and whether any entity uses one has not been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

In February 2026 the finance ministry said the PDRCL platform for local governments' revenue has [a back-office module for local government agents and a market-collector module, Zando collecte](<https://www.finances.gouv.cg/fr/articles/atelier-pdrcl_120226>). In the last twelve months, the platform [passed final validation at Kintélé on 14 February 2026](<https://www.finances.gouv.cg/fr/articles/cloture-atelier-PDRCL_140226>). The state agency ACSI [presented it to the Mayor of Brazzaville on 30 April 2026](<https://acsi.cg/actualites/presentation-de-la-plateforme-pdrcl-a-la-mairie-de-brazzaville-par-lacsi/>). A pilot [was to follow at the Ndjindji central market in Pointe-Noire once municipal staff had been trained](<https://www.vox.cg/lacsi-deploie-la-plateforme-de-dematerialisation-des-recettes-au-marche-central-de-ndjindji/>). No local government has been found recording on it. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

Cape Verde's decentralisation ministry [is bringing a new municipal information system, Simpol, to the municipalities](<https://www.inforpress.cv/en/municipios-ganham-novas-ferramentas-para-arrecadar-mais-impostos>), to support the new property tax from 2027. In the last twelve months, on 28 October 2026 the Directorate-General for Decentralisation said Simpol would be applied in all 22 municipalities from that day. Municipal staff were trained. Before it, the municipal system in use, SIM 2.0, [handles accounting, budget execution and the allocation of revenues and expenses](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/20126/0/ToR_SIMple_Territory_Management.pdf/fe03f815-0452-ffd6-e948-2b00d5623dc3>). No municipality has been found recording payers or payments in Simpol. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

No stage is set. The one source found, on 2020 fiscal data, says local authorities are not empowered to levy taxes and that none of the nine collects its own. No source found says how a local authority keeps any revenue record, and none names a system in preparation. Nothing found is dated since 2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that local governments keep their revenue records on paper, with no system in use.

No stage is set. The one fact found is an audit of 22 communes over 2014 to 2018, which found most had no updated census of their taxable base. It does not speak for the country. The interior ministry put [a computerised system for following each commune's financial position in service from 11 December 2022](<https://algerie-eco.com/2022/12/19/suivi-de-la-situation-financiere-des-communes-mise-en-service-dun-systeme-informatise/>). No source found says how communes keep their revenue records, and none names a revenue system in preparation or on pilot. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that local governments keep their revenue records on paper, with no system in use.

LoGRI's project page says the Computerized Property Tax Administration (CPTA) platform [was developed for three pilot cities in 2016](<https://logri.org/project/ethiopia-property-tax-system-review/>) and [was never fully implemented](<https://logri.org/project/ethiopia-property-tax-system-review/>). In the last twelve months, the Addis Ababa City Government Revenues Bureau [began a property-tax reform pilot in July 2026, covering property identification and valuation](<https://birrmetrics.com/foreign-ministry-asks-diplomatic-missions-for-staff-and-property-records/>). The pilot moves from the land-rent and building-tax arrangement to a value-based property tax. Nothing has been found on what CPTA records or where its record is held. Nor has anything been found on whether any of the three cities still uses it. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

Libreville's pilot platform, launched on 29 July 2025, [is developed by the company GTI Gabon for the city hall](<https://www.gabonreview.com/libreville-enclenche-la-digitalisation-des-recettes-municipales/>). On 3 July 2026 the mayor said [the city has its own operational system digitalising municipal revenue and securing collection](<https://union.sonapresse.com/fr/paiement-numerique-la-mairie-de-libreville-accompagne-le-deploiement-de-madigipaie>). In the last twelve months, on 29 April 2026 Owendo [signed an agreement with the tax directorate to use Digitax for municipal taxes](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-digitax-convention-de-partenariat-entre-la-direction-generale-des-impots-et-la-mairie-dowendo/>). By October 2026 Libreville's E-Tax had recorded over 4,000 transactions. No local government outside Libreville has been found recording. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

[Nine of Ghana's 260 assemblies, 3.5 per cent](<https://copenhagenconsensus.com/sites/default/files/gp_a4_digitization_final.pdf>), used the dLRev revenue software throughout 2019. It [holds a register of businesses and properties with their owners](<https://copenhagenconsensus.com/sites/default/files/gp_a4_digitization_final.pdf>), and has been hosted on the National IT Agency's platform since 2017. In the last twelve months, a [training of 350 staff of 35 Municipal Assemblies](<https://isd.gov.gh/local-government-service-trains-350-municipal-assembly-staff-on-digital-revenue-collection/>) began in February 2026. [About 150 officers in six regions](<https://lgs.gov.gh/ohlgs-equips-municipal-assemblies-with-dlrev-software-to-boost-igf-under-gscsp/>) were trained in July 2026. No figure for assemblies recording in dLRev has been found dated after February 2020. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

[In November 2025 Enabel, the Belgian aid agency, awarded the REVIS project in Mamou](<https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/le-partenariat-centre-ga%C3%AFa_revis-atelier-de-capitalisation-sur-la-activity-7490784325500710912-r9-L>) to a consortium of Global Itec and Le Partenariat. REVIS digitised the census of market traders and motorcycle taxis there, and the collection of their taxes. In the last twelve months, [the consortium reported in August 2026 that Mamou's market revenue had risen fourfold](<https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/le-partenariat-centre-ga%C3%AFa_revis-atelier-de-capitalisation-sur-la-activity-7490784325500710912-r9-L>). Enabel held a workshop on 16 July 2026 on repeating the project in other local authorities. No commune has been found recording its payers outside a donor project, and no source says where the REVIS record is held. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

Basse Area Council [implemented a digital tax register](<https://mofea.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/2024-PFM-Annual-Progress-Report.pdf>) in 2024. The ministry of finance's report of September 2025 names [one council, Basse, as operating the system](<https://mofea.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/SECOND-and-THIRD-QUARTER-PFM-PERFORMANCE-REPORT-1-1.pdf>). In the last twelve months, a UN agency [tendered in June 2026 for a property tax digital management system for Kanifing Municipal Council](<https://www.ungm.org/Public/Notice/304209>). No award has been found. The April 2026 evaluation of the public finance strategy reports the Digital Tax Collection System [largely unimplemented in Banjul City Council](<https://mofea.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/END-EVALUATION-REPORT-OF-THE-PUBLIC-FINANCE-MANAGEMENT-STRATEGY-2021-2025.pdf>). No total of councils has been found beside any count. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

A paper of September 2020 said [thirty-three of the 47 counties, 70 per cent, had automated their revenues, some in part](<https://eujournal.org/index.php/esj/article/view/13419/13560>). A 2018 policy brief had found [most counties that had automated did not own their system](<https://cegkenya.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/Policy-Brief-Brochure2.pdf>). In the last twelve months, standards [gazetted on 27 July 2026, say counties are to own their systems and revenue data](<https://cra.go.ke/download/standards-and-guidelines-on-the-automation-of-county-own-source-revenue/?wpdmdl=5257>). The Vision 2030 Delivery Secretariat's review of 23 February 2026 [names five with well-established systems and cashless collection](<https://vision2030.go.ke/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/ASSESSMENT-REPORT-AUTOMATION-EMPLOYMENT-IN-COUNTIES-23-02-2026.pdf>). No source has been found saying counties hold a register of payers. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

UNDP reported in June 2026 that the firm KWARECOM [runs the Real Property Tax Expansion pilot with UNDP and Sweden](<https://www.undp.org/liberia/press-releases/advancing-fiscal-decentralization-and-local-revenue-liberia>), with the Liberia Revenue Authority. Monrovia City Corporation's Ewallie platform [holds business invoices marked paid or pending](<https://liberianinvestigator.com/townships-say-mcc-owes-18-months-revenue/>). Three neighbouring local governments say they have no access to it. In the last twelve months, a joint mission in June 2026 [visited the pilot in Grand Bassa, Margibi and Nimba](<https://www.undp.org/liberia/press-releases/advancing-fiscal-decentralization-and-local-revenue-liberia>). No local government outside Monrovia has been found recording past a pilot. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

The Ministry of Local Government of the Government of National Unity [runs the National Programme for Activating Local Revenues](<https://alwasat.ly/news/libya/441789>). On 10 June 2024, [27 municipalities signed a sponsorship document committing them to implement the programme](<https://alwasat.ly/news/libya/441789>). Its projects include an electronic collection system and a database of municipal economic activities. The programme director gave no count of municipalities where the local revenue system is activated, and the 27 signatories are not said to use it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

GIR-CT is the integrated revenue management system for local authorities. It was reported on 29 May 2025 as [run by the Interior Ministry's directorate for local authorities with the national treasury](<https://fr.hespress.com/426411-casablanca-settat-mobilisation-des-autorites-pour-renforcer-la-collecte-des-taxes-locales-et-eviter-la-prescription.html>). The World Bank's status report on its mission of August 2025 [puts GIR-CT in place in more than 100 large municipalities](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099091725093035764/pdf/P169330-2f57d0eb-443d-4f4f-8ece-fd23a0d3699f.pdf>). It gives no total of municipalities. The Interior Ministry's circular [had it deployed in 969 of 1,590 local authorities on 19 May 2020](<https://aueks.ma/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Cir-du-Ministre-de-linterieur-N%C2%B0-32-du-19-5-2020-la-mise-en-oeuvre-et-suivi-de-dematerialisation-des-procedures-vers-Zero-papier.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

[In February 2024 Mahajanga commune put two programs into use](<https://www.lexpress.mg/2024/02/commune-urbaine-de-mahajanga-logiciel.html>), SIGRL for local revenue and one for registering taxpayers. They hold each taxpayer's registration, payments and transfer orders. Mahajanga is the one commune outside the capital shown recording its taxpayers. In the last twelve months, [Antananarivo launched the digital collection of market dues on 7 October 2026](<https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202610080562.html>), after registering its market traders on tablets. No share or total of communes recording their payers has been found. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

A Pro-ARIDES note of July 2024 says ReCoDe, the communes' software, was [chosen by the national local finance committee and rolled out by the DGCT and the treasury](<https://proarides.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Pro-ARIDES_2024_NT_Mali_Digitalisation-taxes.pdf>). It was [deployed in 680 communes for testing](<https://proarides.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Pro-ARIDES_2024_NT_Mali_Digitalisation-taxes.pdf>). After training in 27 communes, [only Kava was willing to carry tax digitalisation through](<https://proarides.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Pro-ARIDES_2024_NT_Mali_Digitalisation-taxes.pdf>). In the last twelve months, a project launched on 6 March 2026, starting with Koutiala. It is [to give pilot communes a digital solution and equipment for financial management and the collection of communal taxes](<https://www.idsahel.com/2026/08/13/koutiala-un-projet-de-recensement-fiscal-et-de-digitalisation-pour-renforcer-la-gestion-des-ressources-communales/>). No commune outside Bamako has been found using the local tax module as routine. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

Partners for Water reported in March 2025 that Beira [linked its digitised land registry to its tax collection system](<https://partnersforwater.nl/news/beiras-land-registry-the-key-to-the-system-change-that-will-support-a-climate-resilient-city/>), so the municipality knows who owns what and who must pay property tax. Beira is [the one municipality running the linked registry and tax system](<https://partnersforwater.nl/news/beiras-land-registry-the-key-to-the-system-change-that-will-support-a-climate-resilient-city/>). In Nampula a 2025 case study found [no electronic system for the personal municipal tax](<https://doi.org/10.54751/revistafoco.v18n9-049>). In the last twelve months, on 8 August 2026 CEDSIF, the state's information systems centre, published a page [setting out the e-SGA modules](<https://www.cedsif.gov.mz/cedsifportal/sga/>), which does not say e-SGA is in use. No total of municipalities has been found. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

In April 2025 the Interior Ministry's decentralisation directorate said the El Mouhassil application, [in use since 2020, now serves about 30 municipalities](<https://www.rimtoday.net/?q=node%2F45609>). It gave no total of communes. The mayor of Ksar said in December 2023 that [El Mouhassil runs a full taxpayer census whose data go into the municipal database](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/235987>). Each commune keeps its own record. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The total of communes against which the 30 can be set has not been found. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

The International Growth Centre found in 2022 that revenue management systems had been [introduced in all four city councils since 2017, of 35 local governments](<https://www.theigc.org/sites/default/files/2024-01/Fleck%20et%20al%20Final%20report%20August%202023.pdf>). In Blantyre, Lilongwe and Mzuzu the systems [held property and business owners with their payments and liabilities in one database per city](<https://www.theigc.org/sites/default/files/2024-01/Fleck%20et%20al%20Final%20report%20August%202023.pdf>). In February 2025 the United Nations Development Programme named [one district council, Mwanza](<https://www.undp.org/malawi/stories/digital-tool-improves-how-mwanza-collects-revenue>), with its own system. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No system has been found in the other 30 local governments. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

As reported for February 2024, the City of Windhoek [bills water accounts for named customers in the system it calls Solar](<https://www.namibian.com.na/city-in-water-billing-system-cover-up/>). Payments and arrears are recorded against each account, and the billing system ran on the city's own servers. On 2 July 2024 the city [confirmed irregularities in its water billing system](<https://www.namibian.com.na/city-in-water-billing-system-cover-up/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No local authority outside Windhoek has been found recording revenue, and no total of those recording. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

The City of Niamey launched the Naneye Yarda platform on 3 October 2024 [under its 2025-2027 strategic plan](<https://www.lesahel.org/lancement-du-projet-naneye-yarda-renforcer-la-modernisation-et-lefficacite-des-services-publics-municipaux/>). In January 2026 its administrator said the project [had enumerated 35,000 taxpayers and follows each notice to payment](<https://www.lesahel.org/journee-portes-ouvertes-a-lhotel-de-ville-de-niamey-faire-decouvrir-linstitution-et-expliquer-le-fonctionnement-du-projet-naneye-yarda/>). In the last twelve months, the commune urbaine of Diffa [put the system into service on 11 December 2025](<https://www.undp.org/fr/niger/actualites/diffa-numerise-limpot-local-avec-naneye-yarda>), replacing manual collection and incomplete taxpayer files. No count of communes recording has been found, and nothing reports use in Diffa since. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

In March 2017 [the Edo State government introduced an automated revenue collection system under the Edo Jobs Initiative](<https://www.akamai.university/uploads/1/2/7/7/127725089/pjst19_2_242.pdf>). A journal article of November 2018 describes an app in which [agents register payers, businesses and vehicles and collect and print receipts](<https://www.akamai.university/uploads/1/2/7/7/127725089/pjst19_2_242.pdf>). It says [two of Edo State's local government areas use the system](<https://www.akamai.university/uploads/1/2/7/7/127725089/pjst19_2_242.pdf>), Oredo and Egor. Before it, revenue was collected on manual receipts. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Whether the two still use it, and how many local government areas keep a digital revenue record, has not been found. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

The Sennar state finance ministry [launched Isali electronic collection on 12 May 2026 at the transport and petroleum department and Sinja locality](<https://almndranews.com/88116/>), as reported in May 2026. Sinja was [one of two model sites in Sennar State at the launch](<https://almndranews.com/88116/>). In the last twelve months, that launch [followed preparation from January 2026, in stages of networking, account opening and training](<https://almndranews.com/88116/>). No other locality has been found collecting electronically. Whether collection in Sinja ran past its model stage, whether a register of payers is kept and where the record is held has not been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

The vendor Linking Development states, as at November 2025, that [more than 20 communes in Senegal are equipped with Terlink](<https://www.linking-development.fr/realisations/projet-terlink-la-digitalisation-des-communes-senegalaises/>), its municipal software. It says Terlink [includes accounting and taxation modules covering the recovery and management of communal taxes](<https://www.linking-development.fr/realisations/projet-terlink-la-digitalisation-des-communes-senegalaises/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found on whether any commune uses the software, what it records of payers, or where the record is held. No total of communes beside the count has been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

The Ministry of Finance [runs the rollout with the Ministry of Local Government](<https://mof.gov.sl/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/REoI-for-Tax-System_RUSLP.pdf>), as at May 2026, of the Moptax property tax system. LoGRI says [Moptax runs in Freetown, Kenema and Makeni](<https://logri.org/story/impact-in-sierra-leone/>), and the ministry counts [three of 22 local councils with the upgraded system](<https://mof.gov.sl/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Public-Financial-Management-Report-2025.pdf>) in December 2025. In the last twelve months, Freetown City Council was [upgraded to MOPTAX 2.0 in December 2025](<https://mof.gov.sl/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Public-Financial-Management-Report-2025.pdf>). In May 2026 the ministry [invited firms to roll the system out in Bo and Koidu New Sembehun](<https://mof.gov.sl/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/REoI-for-Tax-System_RUSLP.pdf>). No council beyond the three has been found recording on the system. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

[Four Puntland local governments, Galkacyo north, Garowe, Qardho and Bosaso, used the system to collect taxes](<https://somalipublicagenda.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/SPA_Governance_Briefs_26_2023_ENGLISH.pdf>) in October 2022. In Garowe, Qardho and Galkacyo [properties were mapped and registered in the local government financial system](<https://somalipublicagenda.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/SPA_Governance_Briefs_26_2023_ENGLISH.pdf>), which replaced printed receipts and books. In November 2022 [no local government or district in Galmudug and Benadir had a financial management system](<https://somalipublicagenda.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/SPA_Governance_Briefs_26_2023_ENGLISH.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No total of local governments has been found, so the four are a count and no share. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

In October 2022 [Stateman Software & Telecom Ltd was named as developer, implementer and manager](<https://www.onecitizendaily.com/index.php/2022/10/21/advertisement-by-juba-city-council-jcc/>) of Juba City Council's digital revenue system. A council notice invited businesses to register on it. In the last twelve months, [the Central Equatoria State Government launched a digital revenue collection system and e-services for the council](<https://radioyei.org/news/states/central-equatoria/juba-city/juba-city-council-discusses-digital-revenue-transition/>) in September 2026. In late October 2026 the caretaker mayor said [the council had moved all its revenue operations from manual forms to a digital payment system](<https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/juba-city-council-launches-digital-payment-system-to-improve-transparency>). No council other than Juba City Council has been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

For 2024/2025 the Municipal Council of Manzini [issued rates bills to individual ratepayers by post, email and bulk SMS](<https://manzinicity.co.sz/rates-bills-for-2024-2025-financial-year-now-available/>), on its notice of April 2024. It keeps their contact and ownership details, and ratepayers [check their rates balance and pay](<https://manzinicity.co.sz/rates-bills-for-2024-2025-financial-year-now-available/>) by USSD code. In December 2020 it said [rates had been billed in April 2020](<https://manzinicity.co.sz/you-can-now-pay-rates-using-e-mali/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No local government other than Manzini has been found keeping such a record. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

In April 2025 Mongo began a taxpayer census [run by the commune with the firm IT Solution Center](<https://tchadvision.com/mongo-le-recensement-fiscal-se-modernise-pour-optimiser-la-gestion-des-contribuables-decouvrez-les-enjeux-cles-aujourdhui/>). It is described as the start of a digital tax system recording payments directly. In the last twelve months, on 21 April 2026 N'Djamena [launched digital collection of municipal revenue](<https://journaldutchad.com/tchad-la-commune-de-ndjamena-digitalise-la-collecte-des-recettes/>), starting at the Central Market. A census there had enrolled the first traders. No commune has been found recording payments in a system past launch. Where such a record would be held has not been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

[UNDP and the commune of Lacs 1, at Aného, were said to have initiated a project to digitalise the registration of municipal taxes](<https://www.undp.org/fr/togo/actualites/chaque-nom-compte-la-digitalisation-des-actes-detat-civil-une-experience-du-pnud-dans-les-communes>), after a visit on 27 May 2021. The project belongs to the commune and UNDP. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated after May 2021 has been found, and no start of use is stated for the Lacs 1 project. What is recorded and where it is held has not been found. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

A GIZ study of March 2022 says the commune president [lists the taxable persons and the amounts due](<https://www.giz.de/sites/default/files/media/els-document/2025-08/giz-idm-2203-les-revenus-municipaux-et-les-circuit-paiements-fr.pdf>) for the business tax. The president enters the list in the commune's GRB system. The entry is [visible on the GRB network to the regional treasurer and the municipal receiver of the Ministry of Finance](<https://www.giz.de/sites/default/files/media/els-document/2025-08/giz-idm-2203-les-revenus-municipaux-et-les-circuit-paiements-fr.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the REMO project, which produced GRB 2.0, [ended on 30 April 2026](<https://www.lapresse.tn/2026/05/16/cooperation-tunisie-allemagne-le-projet-remo-prend-fin-en-propulsant-la-gouvernance-locale-a-lere-numerique/>). No count or share of communes entering their rolls in GRB has been found, and no plan naming the system. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

By February 2023 [169 councils had started to use TAUSI](<https://dailynews.co.tz/how-usaid-ps3-project-increased-efficiency-in-govt-systems/>), the minister told the National Assembly. TAUSI is the revenue system run by PMO-RALG. The auditor counts [184 local government authorities](<https://www.nao.go.tz/uploads/Annual_General_Report_for_Audit_of_PO-RALG__Regional_Administrations_and_Local_Government_Authorities_FY_2024-25.pdf>). In 2023/24 [16 of them collected through the older LGRCIS instead](<https://www.nao.go.tz/uploads/Annual_General_Report_for_Audit_of_PO-RALG__Regional_Administrations_and_Local_Government_Authorities_FY_2023-24.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the budget speech of 11 June 2026 [commits the ministry and the revenue authority to finish linking TAUSI to the national tax system](<https://www.mof.go.tz/uploads/text-editor/files/GOVERNMENT%20BUDGET%20%20SPEECH---ENGLISH%20VERSION_1781243659.pdf>). No share of authorities recording in TAUSI has been found since February 2023. Mature would need at least 90 per cent of local governments to keep that register in a national or shared system, on a figure published within two years.

In April 2025 the National Building Review Board said [IRAS ran revenue collection and payment in 166 vote-level local governments](<https://nbrb.go.ug/bims-and-iras-integrated-to-boost-compliance-and-revenue-generation-in-local-governments/>), of the country's 176. In the last twelve months, the finance ministry said in October 2026 that [IRAS holds 3,101,290 registered taxpayers, with bills, payments and arrears](<https://habaridaily.com/the-grizzly-wall-behind-governments-heavy-burden-in-funding-local-governments/>). It also said [it had been rolled out to all of them](<https://habaridaily.com/the-grizzly-wall-behind-governments-heavy-burden-in-funding-local-governments/>). In a sample of 30, the Auditor General [found staff using it but short of skills, connectivity and devices](<https://www.independent.co.ug/system-failures-blamed-for-shs52-billion-local-revenue-shortfall/>). A published share of local governments recording in IRAS has not been found. Mature would need at least 90 per cent of local governments to keep that register in a national or shared system, on a figure published within two years.

National Treasury's budget circular of 7 December 2023 [has each municipality reconcile its valuation roll to its billing system](<https://mfma.treasury.gov.za/Circulars/2024_25%20MTREF%20Budget%20Circular%20No.%20126%20-%2007%20December%202023%20%28final%29.pdf>). It says every municipality's property-rates billing report [holds, for each property, the market value, the category and the amount billed](<https://mfma.treasury.gov.za/Circulars/2024_25%20MTREF%20Budget%20Circular%20No.%20126%20-%2007%20December%202023%20%28final%29.pdf>), with the owner and any rebate. The billing record [stays in the municipality's own billing system](<https://mfma.treasury.gov.za/Circulars/2024_25%20MTREF%20Budget%20Circular%20No.%20126%20-%2007%20December%202023%20%28final%29.pdf>), and the reconciliation goes to the Treasury each quarter. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No count or share of municipalities billing from a system has been found. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.

Smart Zambia, the state digital agency, [announced the e-Council system in March 2026 as part of the national e-government plan](<https://kalemba.news/local/government-to-track-cdf-transactions-payment-digitally-as-e-council-develops/>). In the last twelve months, the first phase is [a proof of concept in eight councils, among them Ndola, Kitwe, Solwezi, Chingola, Kalulushi, Kalumbila and Chilanga](<https://kalemba.news/local/government-to-track-cdf-transactions-payment-digitally-as-e-council-develops/>). A demonstration was expected by 19 June 2026. Before it, a policy brief of May 2024 found [most local councils still run on manual systems](<https://www.theigc.org/sites/default/files/2024-08/Kaputula%20and%20Oliveira-Cunha%20Policy%20brief%20May%202024_1.pdf>). Nothing has been found showing the system live in any council, or the June 2026 demonstration taking place. Establishing would need some local governments outside the capital recording payments in a system, past any pilot.

The Harare Institute of Technology told the Harare Commission of Inquiry in November 2024 that [around 83 of Zimbabwe's 92 local authorities use at least one LADS module](<https://www.heraldonline.co.zw/hit-offers-affordable-erp-system-to-harare/>). For 2024 the Auditor-General found [most local authorities without an ERP system for revenue collection](<https://veritaszim.net/sites/veritas_d/files/Report%20%20of%20the%20Auditor-General%20for%20the%20Year%20Ended%2031%20Dec%202024%20on%20Local%20Authorities.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in June 2026 Gemnation reported [LADS mobile revenue collection deployed to 53 councils](<https://gemnation.co.zw/harare-residents-can-now-score-their-council-in-real-time-heres-how/>). Mutare's Town Clerk said [LADS digital billing had lifted collection efficiency from 33 per cent in 2019 to 65 per cent](<https://www.clgf.org.uk/whats-new/news/cscn-peer-learning-clinic-highlights-mutares-digital-transformation-journey-to-strengthen-municipal-finance/>). Which modules the 83 use has not been found. Operating would need a published share showing more than half keep a digital register of payers.
